title: Lesson 9 · Conjunctions
blurb: Finding conjunctions, conjunction vs preposition, compound subjects/predicates/objects, and the series comma.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“We moved silently and cautiously.”
items.explain: “and” joins the two adverbs — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“He worked hard, but earned little.”
items.explain: “but” joins the two statements — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“I shall not go, if it rains.”
items.explain: “if” joins the two clauses — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“Emma or Susan will stay home.”
items.explain: “or” joins the two subjects — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“They submit, since they cannot win.”
items.explain: “since” joins the two clauses — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“I stayed, because I was tired.”
items.explain: “because” joins the two clauses — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“Study hard, or you will fail.”
items.explain: “or” joins the two clauses — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Which word is the conjunction (the joining word)?

“Salt and pepper spilled.”
items.explain: “and” joins the two subjects — the conjunction.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“and”
items.explain: “and” merely joins and needs no object — a conjunction.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“of”
items.explain: “of” takes an object and shows a relation — a preposition.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“but”
items.explain: “but” merely joins — a conjunction.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“with”
items.explain: “with” takes an object and shows a relation — a preposition.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“if”
items.explain: “if” joins clauses and needs no object — a conjunction.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“under”
items.explain: “under” takes an object and shows a relation — a preposition.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“because”
items.explain: “because” joins clauses and needs no object — a conjunction.

items.prompt:
Is this word a conjunction (only joins) or a preposition (shows relation, has an object)?

“through”
items.explain: “through” takes an object and shows a relation — a preposition.

items.prompt:
Which part is compound (joined by a conjunction)?

“Ellen and Lucy are sisters.”
items.explain: “Ellen and Lucy” are two joined subjects — a compound subject.

items.prompt:
Which part is compound (joined by a conjunction)?

“We run, jump, and play.”
items.explain: “run, jump, and play” are joined verbs — a compound predicate.

items.prompt:
Which part is compound (joined by a conjunction)?

“Dad owns a farm and a factory.”
items.explain: “a farm and a factory” are two joined objects — a compound object.

items.prompt:
Which part is compound (joined by a conjunction)?

“Cats and dogs are pets.”
items.explain: “Cats and dogs” are two joined subjects — a compound subject.

items.prompt:
Which part is compound (joined by a conjunction)?

“She reads and writes well.”
items.explain: “reads and writes” are joined verbs — a compound predicate.

items.prompt:
Which part is compound (joined by a conjunction)?

“He bought apples and pears.”
items.explain: “apples and pears” are two joined objects — a compound object.

items.prompt:
Which is punctuated correctly as a series?

dogs cats birds
items.explain: Commas after each part, and “and” before the last: dogs, cats, and birds.

items.prompt:
Which is punctuated correctly as a series?

red white blue
items.explain: Commas after each part, and “and” before the last: red, white, and blue.
